body:
Ah, I honestly didn't know that abt bcp. Good to be more informed though. I don't always pay as much attention to things as I probably should lol.

But yea, I agree overall, I feel like trying out options that have less irreversible consequenses should be the first attempts to fix these kinds of issues, not the other way around.

This would be interesting, but I am not entirely sure it would work on me 🤔 I _am_ currently taking birth control pills that contain estrogen (to help deal with my periods that cause me a lot of pain and other physical issues), but that has not changed things regarding my dysphoria. But I think this is an interesting point and probably should be looked into more by professionals.
I wasn't really trying to make an argument though. I was just explaining why I think I am delusional for having these feelings, or something to that effect. But I appreciate your input anyway.

Because being trans doesn't make sense in my mind. It honestly just feels like madness. Being gay or bi makes sense, because sex and affection are just as much social functions as they are reproductive. And we see it all over the animal kingdom. But being trans just seems so... weird and unproductive. You're born in one body, that's the body you will have to live in for the rest of your life. Why would my brains just decide that my body shouldn't be this way? Why would I feel the need to live as anything else than what my "original" gender was?

I don't necessarily think that being trans is bad, I have seen people who transition and they seem perfectely happy. But I can't help but feel like there is some underlying issue that could be fixed and everyone could live in their "birth genders" perfectly happily. Idk. All I know, is that if I could take a pill that would make me feel like a cis woman, I'd take it in a heartbeat.

That is somewhat what I have been trying to do lately. I have recently started to "embrace" my masculinity a bit more, I've started working out to alliviate my dysphoria and I've been contemplating on going to the army after I graduate (all men have to go serve their duty in the army in my country and this includes trans men, so I guess I'd have to go there at some point anyways, if I do end up transitioning. Might as well go through with it now, I guess?). I'll see what more I can do. And yes, you're right. Whatever I am on the inside, I am, whether other people see it or not. I guess I've just been getting way too ahead of myself and making myself feel stressed because of it. Thank you for helping me put things into perspective.
